endorsements.quote: Finally, proactive and rigorous bias audits must become a non-negotiable part of this validation process.

Crucially, validation must be co-developed with patients themselves, not only to ensure relevance and accuracy, but to avoid repeating the historical pattern of building tools solely based on expert consensus.

unlisted_practices: Develop new validation methodologies tailored to LLM-based patient-reported outcome assessments rather than relying solely on legacy psychometric techniques.
Adopt a three-tiered validation framework of general, task-specific, and clinical validation for LLM-based PRO tools.
Test whether LLMs can reliably detect clinically meaningful change over time.
Assess test-retest reliability, inter-model consistency, and construct, content, and criterion-related validity of LLM-based PRO assessments.
Conduct comparative studies matching LLM-generated insights with standardized PRO scores and with patient and expert clinical assessments.
Adapt explainability techniques to the specific challenges of LLM applications in healthcare.
Combine LLMs with traditional machine learning techniques to improve interpretability and mitigate clinical risks in PRO tasks.
Provide clinician training and workflow adaptation to accommodate novel forms of patient-reported information from AI.
Include diverse populations in the design and validation of AI-enabled PRO tools.
Be transparent about how AI-generated outputs are produced and used.
Use the Trustworthy and Responsible Ethical Generative AI in Healthcare framework as a reference for developing AI-powered PROs.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary article discussing how generative AI and LLMs can reimagine patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and recommending directions for validation, clinical actionability, equity, and trust.
